vocabulary.definition: for all future time; for always
vocabulary.example: The beauty of the night sky will last forever.

vocabulary.definition: having lost the physical, mental, or moral qualities considered normal and desirable; showing evidence of decline
vocabulary.example: The abandoned house had a degenerate appearance with broken windows and overgrown weeds.
The superhero had the power to annihilate any enemy with a single touch.

vocabulary.definition: involving or causing sudden great damage or suffering
vocabulary.example: The earthquake had a catastrophic impact on the city, leaving buildings in ruins.

vocabulary.definition: in a way that cannot be reversed or undone
vocabulary.example: The decision to sell the family heirloom was irreversible once the contract was signed.

vocabulary.definition: deserving or inviting derision or mockery; absurd
vocabulary.example: The comedian's jokes were so ridiculous that the audience couldn't stop laughing.
